lines.text: Bonus round: why does posting again feel so tempting after a few likes?
That pull is called reward learning.
Researchers tracked more than four thousand people on Instagram and other sites.
Across over a million posts, when likes came in fast, people posted more often.
When likes dried up, they posted less.
It's the same learning that keeps a lab rat pressing a lever for food.
Your feed is training you. Notice who's holding the treats.

post.title: Why Likes Make You Want to Post Again #shorts
post.description: Likes work like treats. Lindström et al. (2021, Nature Communications) analyzed over a million posts from 4,000+ users on Instagram and other sites: people posted more often when likes came in fast and less when they dried up, the same reward learning seen in animals seeking food. #psychology #socialmedia #digitalwellbeing
